thread:
Riya: Hey team — Acme reported console 403 when switching projects this morning after our service-identity rebind. RequestId: req-9b2f, org: acme-org-17. Steps to reproduce: log into console as SSO user, switch org -> 403. Sample curl:

curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/xyz -i
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"permission_denied","message":"missing project.viewer","authz_request_id":"req-9b2f"}

Anyone seen this with service-identity rebinds? @elaine @tom

Elaine: Thanks — can you paste the authz_request_id (you included) and the last 6 of the org id? also is the login a human SSO user or a CI/service account?

Riya: org last6: f3a17c. It's a human SSO user but Acme says their CI service account also had a rebind earlier today. Both are showing 403.

Tom: Seen something similar. When a service identity is rebound we sometimes get a temporary mismatch in idp claims -> principal canonicalization fails and inherited deny rules surface. Two quick asks: 1) can you share the full authz header + request id from the UI network tab? 2) paste the support trace from the console (there's an authz_request_id link in logs).

Riya: Pasting UI error trace (redacted):

--- begin ---
{
  "status": 403,
  "error": "permission_denied",
  "message": "User does not have required role for project switch",
  "authz_request_id": "req-9b2f",
  "hint": "checked bindings: inherited_deny=true for org policy id org-policy-77"
}
--- end ---

deploy-bot: Completed service-identity rebind for org=acme-org-17 at 2026-03-17T03:40:21Z by infra-rotation.

Henry: Can you run the admin binding check?
```
redwood-admin iam get-bindings --org acme-org-17 --principal \"user:riya@acme.com\" --json
```

Riya: Ran it, output:

[
  {
    "binding_id": "b-901",
    "principal": "user:riya@acme.com",
    "role": "project.viewer",
    "scope": "project:xyz",
    "inherited": false
  },
  {
    "binding_id": "b-800",
    "principal": "group:acme-devs",
    "role": "project.viewer",
    "scope": "org:acme-org-17",
    "inherited": true,
    "inherited_deny": true
  }
]

Elaine: That inherited_deny is the problem. Deny rules (org-level) override explicit allows; if the group got an inherited deny via a legacy policy we need to remove that deny or change the principal canonicalization so the user doesn't fall into the denied principal. Two remediation options: 1) temporary support patch to create an explicit allow on the project for user:riya@acme.com, or 2) fix the idp/SCIM sync so group->principal mapping matches post-rebind.

Tom: Quick check — did the rebind change the service identity prefix? We saw group renames during earlier rollouts that caused principal strings to flip (e.g. group:acme-devs -> group:acme-developers). If SCIM hasn't reconciled, the user may still be considered member-of group:acme-devs which now has deny attached.

Riya: Customer confirms they renamed the group earlier today (acme-devs -> acme-developers) and SCIM resync was in progress during the rebind.

Elaine: Ok. Best next step: ask Acme to trigger a SCIM resync for that group. While that's happening we can apply the temporary explicit allow. If you want me to apply the allow I can, but I need approval from support lead (policy).

Riya: Please apply the temporary allow — customer is blocked and it's urgent. RequestId req-9b2f.

Elaine: support-lead approved via DM. Applying patch now.

Elaine: patch applied: created explicit binding allow b-999 for principal user:riya@acme.com role project.viewer scope project:xyz (expires in 2h).

Riya: Customer retested — console project switch successful, no 403. :thumbsup:

Henry: Follow-up: we should add an alert on rebind windows that flags pending SCIM resyncs and potential principal canonicalization mismatches (pre-flight check). I can create a todo in eng-infra.

Tom: Agreed. Also add docs blurb in runbooks: "service-identity rebind + group rename -> possible inherited deny" with remediation steps.

Riya: Root cause summary for ticket: During service-identity rebind a SCIM group rename left group membership in an intermediate state. The org-level deny attached to the old group principal caused users to match an inherited deny. Explicit temporary allow fixed the immediate customer impact; permanent fix: run SCIM resync and audit/remove legacy deny binding.

Elaine: Closing the thread once the SCIM resync completes and deny binding is removed.

Riya: SCIM resync finished and legacy deny binding b-800 was deleted by acme-idp-admin at 2026-03-17T04:10:02Z. Confirmed no further 403s. Thanks everyone.
